To cite the clifford package in publications, use
@hankin2025_clifford.  Here I demonstrate that antivectors are blades
using algebra and give a numerical example.


```{r packageidiom}
library(clifford)

signature(3,4)
n <- 7
options("maxdim" = n)

A <- as.antivector(c(2,3,5,7,11,13,17))
v <- A * pseudoscalar()


f <- function(n){coeffs(v[n])*e(1) - (e(n)^2) * coeffs(v[1])*e(n)}

f(2)
f(3)

c(
    drop(f(2) %.% v),
    drop(f(3) %.% v),
    drop(f(4) %.% v),
    drop(f(5) %.% v),
    drop(f(6) %.% v),
    drop(f(7) %.% v)
)

jj <- f(2) ^ f(3) ^ f(4) ^ f(5) ^ f(6) ^ f(7)

scalarfac <- (coeffs(A[seq_len(n)[-1]]))^(n-2)

candidate <- jj / scalarfac

candidate - A
```

here is a vector that can be used to calculate `e(n)^2`:

```{r}
 c(rep(c(1,-1),times=signature()),rep(0,getOption("maxdim")-sum(signature())))
```
